cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine review October's supplier bills for HANGS Construction.
First it reads the month-end files: the invoice export, the bills already in the books, the vendor list and the policy book.
Now it opens each invoice and matches it to its bill in the books, by vendor and invoice number.
Accounts payable is simply the money a company owes its suppliers, so every bill must match its invoice.
Where a bill and its invoice disagree, the difference stays on screen to be explained.
Then it checks that equipment is booked at its full cost, with delivery, setup and sales tax.
Next it checks that each bill sits on the right job and account, the way that vendor is usually coded.
Then it checks the company, the approver and the W-9 on every bill.
About $91,000 of bills wait for approval.
In all, about $70,000 is misstated in the books. It writes the workpapers and a draft memo.
All done. Fifteen findings on 13 of 28 documents, including a duplicate bill of about $14,600, stopped before it was paid. Nothing was posted or paid; the controller decides every item.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
